# The fuzz targets of the new core's parsers and wire-format handlers (ADR-0040 item 1), checked by
# .github/scripts/fuzz-registry.py in the quality workflow:
#   <directory> <function> <target> [via <entry point>]
#   <directory> <function> exempt <reason>
# A function of the new core whose name looks like a parser's needs a line here: a C function that is
# not static in src/Core, src/Cedar/Node*.c or src/Cedar/ConfigStore*.c, or an exported Go function or
# method of controller/ or ranz-bgp/, the two trees of the one Go module of ranz. The target is a
# libFuzzer target of src/fuzz (C) or a Go fuzz test in the function's package; its source names the
# function, or the entry point it is reached through. The Go fuzz tests listed here are the ones that
# the ranz workflow runs with go test -fuzz.

# The crypto module (CORE-F1 #61)
src/Core  CryptoAeadOpen        fuzz_noise  via NoiseSessionReceive
src/Core  CryptoCertImportPfx   exempt  Windows parses the PFX (PFXImportCertStore), the operator's own certificate file
src/Core  CryptoIdentityImport  exempt  puts a 32-byte private scalar into the key storage provider; parses nothing
src/Core  CryptoIdentityOpen    exempt  opens a node identity key by its name in the key storage provider; reads no peer's bytes

# The session module (CORE-F2 #62): the Noise handshake, the records and the Login
src/Core  NoiseHandshakeRead    fuzz_noise  via NoiseSessionAccept
src/Core  NoiseSessionAccept    fuzz_noise
src/Core  NoiseSessionFinish    fuzz_noise
src/Core  NoiseSessionReceive   fuzz_noise
src/Core  NoiseLoginParse       fuzz_noise
# The flow hash of the tunnel (CORE-S1-2 #68) reads the Ethernet and IP headers of a peer's frame: no parser word
# in its name, listed as a parser
src/Core  NoiseTunnelFlowHash   fuzz_noise

# The peer module (CORE-S5-2 #78): datagrams, envelopes and signals; the STUN messages of ICE on the socket of the layer,
# which libjuice reads (CORE-S5-3 #79, CORE-S5-6 #412): PeerIceInput reads each once with juice_peer_read of the peer mode
# of libjuice (src/Core/3rdparty/juice-peer.c, which this file does not scope) and hands it to the session that it names,
# whose dispatch the seeds of fuzz_peer reach (its fuzz-reach line; CORE-S5-6-R1 #537)
src/Core  PeerInput             fuzz_peer
src/Core  PeerIceInput          fuzz_peer  via PeerInput
src/Core  PeerOpenSignal        fuzz_peer
src/Core  PeerOpen              fuzz_peer  via PeerOpenSignal
src/Core  PeerEnvelopeOpen      fuzz_peer  via PeerOpenSignal
src/Core  PeerSignalDecode      fuzz_peer
# The symmetric-NAT punch (CORE-S5-7 #413): the payload of a punch message, which fuzz_peer also seals as a probe, a message
# of the exchange of nonces and a keepalive, and as a punch offer or answer, for nodes whose punches are open
src/Core  PeerPunchParse        fuzz_peer
src/Core  PeerPunchInput        fuzz_peer  via PeerInput
# The peer sessions of the data datagrams (CORE-H2 #399): the clear header, the handshake messages and the records,
# and the bind challenge
src/Core  PeerRecordParse       fuzz_peer
src/Core  PeerHandshakeParse    fuzz_peer
src/Core  PeerSessionInput      fuzz_peer  via PeerInput
src/Core  PeerInputChallenge    fuzz_peer  via PeerInput
src/Core  PeerKeyOpen           exempt  opens the node's static key by its name in the key storage provider; reads no peer's bytes

# The transport module (CORE-F4 #64): the fallback list and the frames of the session layer
src/Core  TransportParseList     fuzz_transport
src/Core  TransportNoiseReceive  fuzz_transport
src/Core  TransportRead          exempt  hands the read of a stream to the Read procedure of its transport; parses nothing (TransportNoiseReceive reads the frames)
# The TLS transport (CORE-S2-1 #69): the ServerHello among the first records of a TLS server
src/Core  TransportTlsParseHello  fuzz_transport
# The outbound path (SDN-61 #254): what an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy answers, and the proxy list that a PAC script gives
src/Core  TransportProxyParseHttp   fuzz_transport
src/Core  TransportProxyParseSocks  fuzz_transport
src/Core  TransportProxyParseList   fuzz_transport
# The Trojan posture (CORE-S2-2 #70): the first bytes a server with a decoy reads after the TLS handshake, and the
# server name in the ClientHello that a client splits; no parser word in their names, listed as parsers.
# TransportDecoyProxy relays bytes between the prober and the backend and decodes none, so it is not a parser.
src/Core  TransportDecoyIsHandshake   fuzz_transport
src/Core  TransportDecoyAuthenticate  fuzz_transport
src/Core  TransportTlsHelloName       fuzz_transport

# The VXLAN module (SDN-62 #289): the datagrams of VTEPs
src/Core  VxlanInput  fuzz_vxlan
# Geneve in the VXLAN module (SDN-71 #347): the Geneve header of the datagrams of VTEPs of Geneve, with its options
src/Core  VxlanParseGeneve  fuzz_geneve

# The switch module (CORE-S4-1 #74): the frames that the members of a Network send
src/Core  SwitchInput  fuzz_switch
# The IP table of the switch (SDN-50-N #492) reads the IPv4 header, the ARP packet or the IPv6 header of each frame that the
# ingress of the switch takes; no parser word in the name, listed as the reader of frames that it is
src/Core  SwitchIpLearn  fuzz_switch  via SwitchInput

# The policy engine (CORE-S4-2 #75): the JSON documents of rules, and the frames that the members of a Network send.
# PolicyNewDoc and PolicySetRules have no parser word in their names and are listed as the parsers they are.
src/Core  PolicyParseRules  fuzz_policy
src/Core  PolicyNewDoc      fuzz_policy  via PolicyParseRules
src/Core  PolicySetRules    fuzz_policy
src/Core  PolicyInput       fuzz_policy
# The compiled rule tables of a document as text (CORE-S4-3 #76): no parser word in its name, and it parses the document
src/Core  PolicyTableText   fuzz_policy

# The front door (SDN-29 #205): the first bytes that any peer sends to TCP 443, and the handoff message that an owner
# process reads from its pipe. FrontDoorRoute has no parser word in its name and reads the same bytes.
src/Core  FrontDoorParseHello     fuzz_frontdoor
src/Core  FrontDoorRoute          fuzz_frontdoor
src/Core  FrontDoorHandoffDecode  fuzz_frontdoor

# The control stream of a node (SDN-3 #179; AUD1-DT-12 #460): the messages that the Controller sends, which the node decodes
# with nanopb (ControlDecode) and takes (ControlInput); it applies an Update to the desired state that it holds
# (ControlApply), which has no parser word in its name and is listed as the reader of the Update that it is
src/Core  ControlInput   fuzz_control
src/Core  ControlDecode  fuzz_control  via ControlInput
src/Core  ControlApply   fuzz_control  via ControlInput
# The Relay objects of a state and the Signals that the Controller carries (CORE-S5-5 #411): ControlInput hands an Update to
# ControlCopyRelays and a Signal to ControlTakeSignal, and the frames of TestRelaysAndSignals in the corpus of fuzz_control hold
# both; neither name has a parser word, both are listed as the readers of the controller's bytes that they are
src/Core  ControlCopyRelays  fuzz_control  via ControlInput
src/Core  ControlTakeSignal  fuzz_control  via ControlInput
# The session profiles of a state (SDN-40 #233): ControlInput hands an Update to ControlCopyProfiles, which takes the
# SessionProfile of the NodeConfig and of each Peer object, and the owner of fuzz_control checks what it took. No parser word
# in the name, listed as the reader of the controller's bytes that it is
src/Core  ControlCopyProfiles  fuzz_control  via ControlInput
# The security of the L2 Networks of a state (SDN-41 #234): ControlInput hands the Network objects of an Update to
# ControlCopySecurities, which copies the L2Security of each L2 Network, and the seeds security-*.bin of fuzz_control hold
# them; no parser word in the name, listed as the reader of the controller's bytes that it is
src/Core  ControlCopySecurities  fuzz_control  via ControlInput
# The BGP peering of the standard mode of a state (SDN-77 #357): ControlInput hands the Vrf, NodeConfig and Peer objects of an
# Update to ControlCopyPeerings, which copies the peering of each, and the seeds peering-*.bin of fuzz_control hold them; no
# parser word in the name, listed as the reader of the controller's bytes that it is
src/Core  ControlCopyPeerings  fuzz_control  via ControlInput
# The live operations of the Controller (SDN-50-N #492): ControlInput hands an Operation that ControlDecode decoded to
# ControlTakeOperation, which checks its kind, its Network and the sizes of its MAC address and its address before the owner
# does it, and the seeds operation-*.bin of fuzz_control hold Operations of every kind after a state with L2 and L3 Networks;
# no parser word in the name, listed as the reader of the controller's bytes that it is
src/Core  ControlTakeOperation  fuzz_control  via ControlInput

# The Node and the configuration store of Cedar (CORE-F5)
src/Cedar  NodeParseRoles       exempt  the role names of the node's own configuration, split by ParseToken and looked up in a fixed table
src/Cedar  CsOpen               exempt  opens the node's own SQLite store (winsqlite3)
# The config importer of CORE-F5 (AUD1-DT-12 #460): Cfg parses the bytes of the file (fuzz_cfg) and the importer walks the
# parsed tree into a store
src/Cedar  CsImportForkConfig   fuzz_configimport
src/Cedar  NodeOverlayInput     exempt  a packet of the host's own IP stack on the overlay adapter of a VRF (SDN-3 #179, merged before the gate; SDN-4 #180; SDN-6 #182): NodeNatEnds (fuzz_nat) reads its two addresses as the overlay sees them, the forwarding table of the VRF looks them up, and NodeNatCopy (fuzz_nat) writes the packet after the VRF id, which the policy of the VRF (NodePolicy.c; SDN-8 #184) hands to PolicyInput (fuzz_policy); a fuzz target of its own is still to come
# The 1:1 NAT and 4via6 of the Node (SDN-6 #182) read the packets of the host and of the peers, ICMP errors and the
# packets they quote among them: no parser word in their names, listed as the readers of packets that they are
src/Cedar  NodeNatEnds     fuzz_nat
src/Cedar  NodeNatCopy     fuzz_nat
src/Cedar  NodeNatInbound  fuzz_nat
# The shaping of the overlay (SDN-20 #196) reads the packet of the host that NodeOverlayInput copied: no parser word in
# its name, listed as a parser
src/Cedar  NodeShapeOutput      exempt  only AdjustTcpMssL3 of TcpIp reads the bytes, to clamp the MSS of a TCP SYN, and fuzz_tcpip drives it through AdjustTcpMssL2; the rate limits take the size of the packet alone
# The Mirrors of the Node (SDN-23 #199) read the packets that the overlay sends to the peers and delivers to the host:
# the IPv4 header, the IPv6 extension headers and the ports. No parser word in the name, listed as a parser
src/Cedar  NodeMirrorCopy  fuzz_mirror
# The session profiles of the Node (SDN-40 #233) read the packets that the overlay sends to a peer and takes from one, and
# the ones that the hub of a VRF sends on from one peer to another: the two addresses, the IPv6 extension headers and the
# flags of TCP. No parser word in the names, listed as the readers of packets that they are
src/Cedar  NodeProfileOutbound  fuzz_nodeprofile
src/Cedar  NodeProfileInbound   fuzz_nodeprofile
src/Cedar  NodeProfileTransit   fuzz_nodeprofile
# The hub of a VRF of topology hub-and-spoke judges the packets that it sends on from one spoke to another by the policy of the
# VRF (SDN-19-R2 #508). No parser word in the name, listed with the reason that it is no parser
src/Cedar  NodePolicyTransit  exempt  hands the packet that a spoke sent, as it came, to PolicyInput (fuzz_policy), which parses it, with the members of its two peers; it reads only the two addresses of the IPv4 or IPv6 header within the size of the packet, to find a WireGuard Device, as NodePolicyInbound does for every packet of a peer
# The DHCP responder of an L2 Network (SDN-43 #236) reads the frames that the members of the switch of the Network send:
# the DHCP messages of the clients and of a DHCP server of the LAN, and the ARP requests
src/Cedar  NodeDhcpInput  fuzz_nodedhcp
# The gateway HA of the Node (SDN-19 #195) reads the control records that a peer sends on its Noise session as a probe or
# its answer, and the IP packets of the host whose flow hash picks the gateway of a flow. NodeGatewayFlowHash has no parser
# word in its name, listed as the reader of packets that it is; NodeGatewayControl hands a record to NodeGatewayParseProbe.
# The records of the datagram path of the peer agent carry a probe or its answer behind the VRF tag of no VRF (SDN-19-R1
# #507): NodeGatewayDatagram hands each record to NodeGatewayParseDatagram, which reads that header and hands the rest to
# NodeGatewayParseProbe.
src/Cedar  NodeGatewayParseProbe     fuzz_gateway
src/Cedar  NodeGatewayParseDatagram  fuzz_gateway
src/Cedar  NodeGatewayFlowHash       fuzz_gateway
# The stub resolver of overlay DNS (SDN-11 #187) reads the DNS queries that reach UDP port 53 of the node's addresses in a
# VRF. No parser word in the name, listed as the parser it is
src/Cedar  NodeDnsAnswer  fuzz_nodedns
# The mimicry sidecar of the Node (CORE-P2-6 #406): the messages of its control pipe, and the line in front of each stream
# of its data pipes (the binding of the server role, the answer to a dial of the client role)
src/Cedar  NodeMimicParseMessage  fuzz_nodemimic
src/Cedar  NodeMimicParseBind     fuzz_nodemimic
src/Cedar  NodeMimicParseAnswer   fuzz_nodemimic
# The Capabilities of the Node (ONE-3 #312) come from the host, not from a peer
src/Cedar  NodeCapsReadHost     exempt  reads no bytes of a peer or of a file: it asks Windows for the architecture of the host, whether the services SeLow and xdp are registered and whether three files of System32 exist
# The peer agent of the overlay (CORE-S5-5 #411) takes the Signals that the Controller carries from a peer: no parser word in the
# name, listed as the reader of a peer's bytes that it is
src/Cedar  NodeAgentSignal  exempt  hands the envelope of a Signal as it came to PeerOpenSignal (fuzz_peer), which opens and decodes it; it reads only what that gave
# The internet exit of the Node (SDN-12 #188) reads the IPv4 packets that the peers of a VRF send to an address outside it,
# gives the TCP segments and UDP datagrams of the proxy other ends and writes echo replies. NodeEgressRewrite,
# NodeEgressEchoReply and NodeEgressRefuses have no parser word in their names, listed as the writers and readers of a peer's
# bytes that they are; NodeEgressDeliver and NodeEgressFromHost read only what NodeEgressParse gives.
src/Cedar  NodeEgressParse      fuzz_egress
src/Cedar  NodeEgressRewrite    fuzz_egress
src/Cedar  NodeEgressEchoReply  fuzz_egress
src/Cedar  NodeEgressRefuses    fuzz_egress
src/Cedar  NodeEgressDeliver    exempt  reads the version and the destination of a packet of a peer only once it holds the 20 bytes of an IPv4 header, then hands it to NodeEgressParse (fuzz_egress) and the copy that goes to the host to NodeEgressRewrite (fuzz_egress)
src/Cedar  NodeEgressFromHost   exempt  a packet of the host's own IP stack, which it hands to NodeEgressParse (fuzz_egress) and, when it answers a flow of the proxy, to NodeEgressRewrite (fuzz_egress); it reads no byte that NodeEgressParse did not check
# The bridge of the L2 adapter (CORE-S3-3 #73) looks at each frame of the wire that its XDP backend takes: no parser word in the
# name, listed as the reader of the bytes of the LAN that it is
src/Cedar  NodeL2BridgeWay  exempt  compares the first six bytes of a frame, its destination MAC address, with the address of the NIC and tests their group bit; it reads no length and no field beyond them, and a frame shorter than six bytes is not read
# The EVPN of a gateway node (SDN-25 #201): the learned and withdrawn messages of its BGP sidecar as IP prefix routes of an
# EVPN VRF, and the frames that the VTEPs of a fabric send on the L3 VNI of an EVPN VRF, with the two ends of their packets.
# The functions that take what these read are listed too, as the readers of routes and packets that they are. A frame comes
# in only from a VTEP that the gateway knows for its VRF (SDN-25-R1 #549): NodeEvpnSortVteps sorts the VTEPs of the routes
# that the sidecar gave, and NodeEvpnHasVtep looks the outer source of each frame up among them, no parser word in their names.
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnParseRoute      fuzz_evpn
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnParseFrame      fuzz_evpn
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnEnds            fuzz_evpn  via NodeEvpnParseFrame
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnSortVteps       fuzz_evpn
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnHasVtep         fuzz_evpn
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnRoute           exempt  puts the route that NodeEvpnParseRoute (fuzz_evpn) read from a message of the node's own sidecar into the list of the routes; it reads no byte itself
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnOutput          exempt  a packet of the host's own IP stack, whose two ends NodeNatEnds (fuzz_nat) reads as for NodeOverlayInput, and which NodeNatCopy (fuzz_nat) writes into the frame for the fabric
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnTransit         exempt  a packet of a peer that the overlay delivered, whose two ends NodeEvpnEnds (fuzz_evpn) reads, and which the session profile (NodeProfileInbound, fuzz_nodeprofile) and the policy of the VRF (fuzz_policy) judge before it goes to the fabric as it came, and NodeMirrorCopy (fuzz_mirror) copies
src/Cedar  NodeOverlayFabricInput  exempt  a packet of the fabric that NodeEvpnParseFrame (fuzz_evpn) took, whose two ends NodeOverlayEnds reads as for NodeOverlayDeliver; NodeNatInbound (fuzz_nat) translates it for the host, or NodeNatEnds and NodeNatCopy (fuzz_nat) and the policy (fuzz_policy) take it on to a peer as for NodeOverlayInput
# The MAC addresses and the addresses of the messages of the sidecar, which the stretch of a gateway reads with them too
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnParseMac        fuzz_evpn  via NodeEvpnParseRoute
src/Cedar  NodeEvpnParseAddr       fuzz_evpn  via NodeEvpnParseRoute
# The stretch of a gateway node (SDN-64 #291): the stretch messages of its BGP sidecar, the type-2 and type-3 routes of the
# fabric on the L2 VNI of a stretch, and the frames that the VTEPs of the fabric send on that VNI
src/Cedar  NodeStretchParseRoutes  fuzz_evpn
src/Cedar  NodeStretchInput        exempt  a frame that VxlanInput (fuzz_vxlan) took on the L2 VNI of a stretch, from a VTEP that the gateway knows for the VNI by the routes that NodeStretchParseRoutes (fuzz_evpn) read; it reads no byte of the frame and hands it to SwitchInput (fuzz_switch), the ingress of the switch of the Network

# The credential file of the store (AUD1-DT-8 #456): the JSON that rqlited reads, which the controller wrote itself or an
# operator copied from the first member of a cluster
controller/internal/sidecar  ReadCredential  FuzzParseCredential via parseCredential

# The secrets of the export and audit targets that the store keeps sealed to a key of the controller (AUD1-DT-10 #458), and
# the PresharedKeys of the WireGuard Devices (SDN-82 #377): the bytes that the store holds in place of a sealed secret,
# which anyone who can write to the store can choose
controller/internal/keys  Sealer.Open  FuzzSealerOpen

# The Cluster key of a controller cluster (AUD1-DT-16 #501): the text of the copy of the key in the row of a member, which
# the store reads, and the bytes of the copy, which a member opens with its own sealing key at its start and after; anyone
# who can write to the store can choose both. Keeper.Open opens the secrets of the targets and the PresharedKeys of the
# Devices as the Sealer of a store
controller/internal/store       Store.ClusterKey  FuzzDecodeCopy  via decodeCopy
controller/internal/clusterkey  Keeper.Start      FuzzOpenCopy    via openCopy
controller/internal/clusterkey  Keeper.Open       exempt  opens a sealed secret of a target or a sealed PresharedKey of a Device with the Sealer of the Cluster key (keys.Sealer.Open), which FuzzSealerOpen drives

# The CA certificate and key files of `ranz cert -signcert` and -signkey (SDN-53 #246): the operator's own files, which
# LoadAuthority reads as PEM
controller/internal/certgen  LoadAuthority  FuzzLoadAuthority

# The certificate of the controller (SDN-92 #397): the setting that an operator gives ranz controller-cert set and the API,
# and the PEM files of its file source, which loadPEM reads: the operator's own files, refused with a reason or taken
controller/internal/servercert  ParseSetting  FuzzParseSetting
controller/internal/servercert  Manager.Load  FuzzLoadPEM  via loadPEM

# The file of the data directory that holds the TLS fingerprint of the certificate in use (AUD1-DT-13 #461), which ranz on
# the same host reads before it sends a token to a loopback address: the Controller wrote it itself, or someone replaced it.
# On Windows ranz opens it itself, checks who may have written it and reads it through that handle (AUD1-DT-14 #496).
controller/internal/servercert  ReadFingerprint      FuzzReadFingerprint  via parseFingerprint
controller/internal/servercert  ReadFingerprintFile  FuzzReadFingerprint  via parseFingerprint
controller  ReadFingerprint  exempt  checks who owns and may write the fingerprint file of a data directory of this host and its folder, then reads the file with servercert.ReadFingerprintFile, whose parser FuzzReadFingerprint drives

# The traffic test of `ranz test throughput` (SDN-53 #246): what a peer sends to a test server (the request, and the frames
# of an upload) and to a test client (the frames of a download, the report of an upload)
controller/internal/throughput  ReadRequest     FuzzRead
controller/internal/throughput  ReadReport      FuzzRead
controller/internal/throughput  Receiver.Input  FuzzRead

# The diagnostics bundle (SDN-54 #247): the text of a log and the JSON documents of a bundle, which Redact and RedactJSON read
# before anything leaves the host
controller/internal/bundle  Redact      FuzzRedact
controller/internal/bundle  RedactJSON  FuzzRedactJSON

# The pipe protocol of the BGP sidecar (CORE-S7-1 #82)
ranz-bgp/internal/sidecar  Reader.Read  FuzzRead

# The mimicry sidecar (CORE-P2-1 #85): the messages that the node writes into its control pipe, and the frames that the
# other sidecar sends through the TLS session (frameConn reads them through frameReader)
controller/internal/mimic  Reader.Read       FuzzRead
controller/internal/mimic  frameReader.Read  FuzzFrame
controller/internal/mimic  frameConn.Read    FuzzFrame  via frameReader
